name: Tomás Eiguchi-Brennan
description: Tomás Eiguchi-Brennan is the public face of Axiom Biosynth, one of GLMZ's dominant geneware corponations, known for his signature bioluminescent amber skin-modification — a product placement that glows subtly in low light. Originally a Tier 3 med-school dropout turned minor feed personality, he was talent-scouted by Axiom's brand division in 2214 and given a full cosmetic geneware suite in exchange for a 12-year exclusivity contract he later claimed to not have fully read. His face appears on approximately 40% of Axiom's physical and digital advertising in M88.
cultural_impact: Tomás made bioluminescent skin modifications aspirational for the Tier 3 market, driving a 300% increase in Axiom's cosmetic geneware sales between 2215 and 2219. His visible ambivalence about his contract — expressed in carefully worded feed-posts that stop just short of criticism — has made him a symbol of the ethical gray zone of corporate-contracted celebrity.
key_figures: Yael Okonkwo-Sattler (Axiom Brand VP, his handler)
Renna Cho-Marcelino (his personal attorney, rumored to be trying to find contract loopholes)
locations: Lux Clinic, Tier 3 (Axiom's flagship geneware boutique)
story_hooks: Tomás reaches out to a journalist through a dead-drop in the Underworld — he's found a clause in his contract that suggests Axiom has legal ownership of any genetic data derived from his modified body, and he wants out before a scheduled 'upgrade' procedure.

A Shelf-based bio-pirate collective has reverse-engineered the bioluminescent modification from secondhand genetic samples and is selling unlicensed versions; Axiom wants Tomás to publicly condemn them, but he refuses — the underground version is safer.
Someone has been impersonating Tomás at Tier 1 ghost markets, selling counterfeit Axiom products using his face and amber glow — but the impostor's modifications are better than the real product.
platform: Axiom Brand Network / personal feed on CorporaStream
follower_count: 11.2 million across corporate and personal feeds
controversy: In 2221 he posted a feed that showed him staring at his glowing hand for 47 seconds without caption — the clip was viewed 9 million times and sparked widespread debate about whether it was a cry for help, performance art, or a carefully calculated bid for sympathy that Axiom itself orchestrated.
